text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:

- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says he was furious when he heard of United States government interference in Singapore elections, referring to State Department comments on his People's Action Party (PAP)'s strategy of linking voter support to housing upgrading.
- Singapore Ministry of Foreign Affairs says State Department comments are undisguised interference in Singapore domestic politics.
- United States has no intention of getting involved in Singapore domestic election campaign, U.S. Embassy spokesman says.
- PAP leaders say there is a clear difference between PAP method of selecting candidates and that of opposition.
- United Overseas Bank (UOB) to merge two Malaysian units and form broking venture.
- UOB sees better growth this year than in 1995.
- South East Asia Property Co teams up with President Park Properties of Thailand to tap opportunities in serviced apartments sector in region.
- Stock markets in Japan, South Korea and Thailand pummelled as variety of factors peak investor concerns about local economies.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- International Business Machines Corp will hire hundreds of infotech professionals from early next year to meet high demand for services in Asia.
- Yen falls below 115 to U.S. dollar for first time in nearly four years.
- Property group Malayan Credit Ltd plans to change name and logo as part of overall strategy to revitalise company.
- Diary maker Nippecraft Ltd announces one-for-four rights issue at 28 cents each to raise Singapore $13.75 million to repay bank loans.
- Singapore Press Holdings share price rises 10 cents in reaction to news it could reap extraordinary gain of S$458 million from proposed sales of properties.
- Electronic Resources Ltd proposes to turn Chinese joint venture into full subsidiary to enjoy full benefits of China market.
- OUB Centre to buy S$31 million freehold site in MacPherson Industrial Estate.
- Asiamatrix Ltd calls extraordinary general meeting on proposal to sell leasehold site and machinery and buy smallish plastic engineering firm.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
